stories.teaser: A plant-based food from local crops to treat child malnutrition
stories.headline: Hebrew University researchers develop a plant-based malnutrition treatment made from locally grown crops
stories.why: Published in Current Developments in Nutrition; promising results in rats, with clinical trials still needed.
texts:
Treating malnutrition with what grows nearby.

Hebrew University researchers led by Dr. Aurélie Bechoff developed ChSMS, a therapeutic food made from chickpea, sorghum, maize and soybean instead of imported powdered milk and peanuts. In a study in rats, it supported better recovery than a commercial formula.

“Access is one of the biggest challenges in treating childhood malnutrition,” says Prof. Efrat Monsonego-Ornan.

#Israel #HebrewUniversity #GlobalHealth #Nutrition

Only about 30% of children who need treatment for severe acute malnutrition receive it.

A Hebrew University team wants to change that with a ready-to-use therapeutic food made from local crops: chickpea, sorghum, maize and soybean. It gets about 14% of its energy from protein, versus 10% for a commercial product, with a protein quality score of 87% versus 69%. The early results come from rats; clinical trials are still needed.

#Israel #HebrewUniversity #GlobalHealth #Nutrition

What if malnutrition treatment didn’t depend on imported milk powder?

Researchers at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem tested a plant-based alternative made from chickpea, sorghum, maize and soybean. In rats, it supported catch-up growth and better recovery than a peanut-and-milk formula. The findings, published in Current Developments in Nutrition, still need confirmation in clinical trials.

#Israel #HebrewUniversity #GlobalHealth #Nutrition
